vulnerability_mechanism.evidence: The repository security advisory GHSA-jm78-9fvv-mhgr identifies caller-controlled option names reaching set/set_value/add_value, an option-label validator that rejects only CR/LF/NUL, and write_section serializing the key verbatim as `\t%s = %s\n`. At tag 3.1.57 the local source independently shows that exact entry-check-sink chain. Serializing `sshCommand = printf W012 #` in the sink's format and asking git-config for core.sshCommand returns `printf W012`, confirming directive forgery.

atomic_bic.evidence: Bounded reverse -S searches for both the exact fp.write format and `%s = %s` first reach 3fd37230e76a014cf5c45d55daf0be2caa6948b7. Its lib/git/config.py diff directly implements write_section and first writes the vulnerable key interpolation; later occurrences are moves, removals, or rewrites of the already-existing sink.

immediate_parent_absence.evidence: The BIC has exactly one parent. The parent's lib/git/config.py contains only a no-op write() skeleton; parent-tree grep finds neither write_section nor the tabbed key/value format, while both appear in the BIC tree. The vulnerable serialization is therefore absent from the immediate parent.

squash_member_decomposition.evidence: 3fd37230e76a014cf5c45d55daf0be2caa6948b7 is a single-parent 2009 implementation commit, not a merge or a path-move carrier. Its parent boundary directly brackets first introduction, and no finer public member is present to decompose; the later cb68eef0865df6aedbc11cd81888625a70da6777 path move is 100% rename-only and is not the BIC.

affected_fixed_release_membership.evidence: The published repository advisory declares GitPython <=3.1.57 vulnerable and >=3.1.58 patched. Peeled tags are 3.1.57=ccbd573ac4ab52ccdcf395c400e600d5809bcc88 and 3.1.58=30be45d786e95023e23c616fec5cbabca861b44c. The BIC is an ancestor of both; fix a495ccd3b547ccd60b2187215823b72a9c0188bf is not an ancestor of 3.1.57 and is an ancestor of 3.1.58.

direct_fix_or_unpatched.evidence: The single-parent fix adds VALID_CONFIG_OPTION_NAME_RE and rejects non-fullmatching option names in _assure_config_name_safe before the unchanged writer sink, with regression tests for equals, comments, brackets, whitespace, colon, quotes, and backslash. It is the only git/config.py option-name fix in the 3.1.57..3.1.58 release delta.

bic_only_ai_attribution.evidence: AI attribution was evaluated only on BIC 3fd37230e76a014cf5c45d55daf0be2caa6948b7: author and committer are Sebastian Thiel <byronimo@gmail.com>, timestamp 2009-10-19, and the complete commit message has no AI/co-author/generated/assisted marker. The GPT 5.6 Assisted-by and Co-authored-by trailers are on the 2026 fix only and were excluded from causal attribution.

findings: The primary mechanism, atomic introducer, immediate-parent boundary, release topology, and direct-fix identity independently replay against the authoritative advisory and assigned clone.

The 2026 CR/LF/NUL validator 54538428f79b0c91ba52cda5229856a6edf7ac06 and section-only delimiter validator 1ed1b924f4e2d2ee7bab296df77b978af21853f1 leave equals/hash/whitespace option names accepted; neither is the first writer of this flaw.
The primary NOT_AI verdict is supported by BIC-only evidence; AI markers on the fix do not transfer to the 2009 vulnerable-line writer.
